title: Computer Engineering Technology
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 30S/45Q to fewer than 60S/90Q units

program.section_heading: Computer Engineering Technology Associate of Science Degree
outcomes: Be prepared to transfer a core curriculum to an accredited, 4-year college or university with junior class standing in electronics technology or a related major.
Select and operate electronic test equipment during troubleshooting and repair operations, with an emphasis on safety in use and accuracy in results.
Analyze, interpret, and trace digital logic diagrams used in signal tracing of complex digital computer circuits.
Effectively communicate with and advise customers and co-workers, both written and orally, regarding the progress of and decisions made concerning test and repair procedures.
Sit for industry/Federal-style examinations on the theory and procedures of computer technology.

notes: The source page is the Computer Engineering Technology A.S. degree page, not the Certificate of Achievement page. The degree text says students 'must complete all requirements for the certificate ... plus the general breadth requirements for the Associate Degree (minimum total = 60 units)', so the 38-unit course list was read as the certificate's requirements. A reviewer should confirm this against the certificate page.
The 60-unit minimum and the GE patterns (SBVC GE, Cal-GETC) apply to the A.S. degree only, so degree_total and ge_pattern were left null for the certificate.

The program learning outcomes come from the degree page's outcomes tab and appear to be shared by the program. The first outcome (transfer preparation) reads as degree-oriented; please verify that the certificate shares these outcomes.
The catalog prints TECALC 087, which was matched to closed-list TECALC 87 (same course, leading zero).
ELECTR 230 Semiconductor Devices (3) is not in the closed list, so it is flagged as a catalog addition.
